description:
FILED s515a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-11) from the #3063 acceptance (the 6 rows of t/67_emptrow.t left after the hang fix; PRE-EXISTING on the base 8c683ae6).

    use Text::CSV qw(csv);   # PERL5LIB=cpan-tests/modules/Text-CSV-2.04/lib
    # FILE = "a,b,c,d\n1,2,0,4\n"
    my $r = csv(auto_diag => 0, in => FILE, bom => 1);
    print join(",", sort keys %{$r->[0]}), "\n";
perl: a,b,c,d.  PCL: SCALAR(0x1) (one key).  Without bom => 1 the keys are right.  Probe: scratch/s515a/pr/m3h0.pl in the s515a worktree.  Next step: Text::CSV_PP::header with bom (the BOM-sniff path reads the first line through a scalar ref / in-memory handle).

=== DONE (s516b) ===
MINIMIZED: not Text::CSV and not the BOM -- `my $r = \$s; open my $fh, '<', $r` opened the reference's WRAPPER box, so the handle read the text "SCALAR(0x1)", and the write modes never reached $s.  The written-in-place `\$s` and an array element holding the ref were right: a ref arrives as the wrapper itself OR as a variable holding it, and %p-open-impl read one level down for both.  Fix (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp %p-open-impl): ask %p-scalar-referent-p / %p-ref-referent, the runtime's one reading of both depths.  Text::CSV_PP::header reads its header line exactly this way, so csv(..., bom => 1) keyed every row by "scalar(0x1)".
Acceptance: the probe prints perl's a=1,b=2,c=0,d=4 rows; t/67_emptrow.t alone 56/0 = perl; its six blessed #3202 rows left baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit.  Guard Pl/t/open-modes-01.t 6 -> 7 rows (var read, literal read, in a sub, var write, var append, array element, ref-to-ref; compared with perl's output), inverse-verified on main.
subject: Text::CSV csv(in => FILE, bom => 1) builds its header keys as 'SCALAR(0x..)' -- every row's hash is keyed by a stringified scalar ref (Text-CSV 67_emptrow.t H rows)
